title: Signal Visor protocol definition
description: Declarative description of a sub-GHz protocol. Data only: no scripts and no expressions, so definitions can be distributed as content rather than code. A frame is a string of symbols; for binary protocols the alphabet is {0,1} and a symbol is a bit, for tri-state chips it is {0,1,F}. Field offsets index symbols.

schema.description: Definition format version. A newer value than the application supports makes it skip the definition and ask the user to update.

id.description: Stable slug, unique across the library.

status.description: 'verified' means real captures prove the definition decodes, and the tests that show it run with every build of the application; the evidence itself is kept in the application repository, not in this file. Timing copied from a datasheet stays 'draft' until a real capture proves it.

classification.description: Drives what the application tells the user: a rolling code cannot be interpreted beyond its visible parts.

type.description: PWM and PPM are described by symbols; MANCHESTER, DMC (Differential Manchester) and NRZ are line codes; PCM is a plain clocked bitstream already handed back by an FSK or PSK symbol decoder, with no mark/space pattern of its own.

te_us.description: Base timing element in microseconds. For PWM and PPM the symbol patterns are multiples of it; for Manchester it is the half-bit duration. For PCM there is no pulse to measure, so this is documentary only, but still a positive value.

tolerance.description: Accepted relative timing error, 0.3 meaning plus or minus 30 percent.

te_range_us.description: For chips whose clock is set by an external resistor (EV1527, PT2262): the range the timing element takes across devices, [min, max] in microseconds. Within it the element is no evidence for or against the protocol; te_us is then only a typical value and must lie inside the range.

invert.description: True when the chip transmits mark and space inverted.

symbols.description: Symbol name to timing pattern in TE units, alternating mark (positive) and space (negative). A pattern may hold several pairs, which is how a tri-state chip encodes one trit.

pattern.description: Timing pattern in TE units with alternating signs. Unlike a data symbol it may start with a space, because many protocols separate frames with a long gap and no sync pulse, e.g. [-36]. Used by pulse-based coding types.

bits.description: Fixed 0/1 bit pattern marking the start of a frame inside a PCM bitstream, e.g. a sync word such as "0010110111010100". Used only when coding.type is PCM.

polarity.description: Manchester transition polarity; DMC uses ieee (start transition is 0) or thomas (start transition is 1).

length.description: Number of data symbols in one frame (bits, for a binary alphabet).

format.description: 'raw' is the only format valid for a non-binary alphabet.

role.description: What the field means, so the interface and exports can treat it sensibly.

check.description: Checksum or CRC over part of the frame. Requires a binary alphabet. Every CRC parameter is open so the solver can search this space.

at.description: First symbol of the stored check value.

flipper.description: Flipper Zero protocol name, when its firmware knows this protocol.

tests.description: One entry per test case proving the definition. A shared definition usually carries only the count (empty objects); which capture and which values each entry stands for is kept in the application repository, matched by position. At least one entry is required before status may become 'verified'.

file.description: Sample capture, when this project owns one: a path relative to the definition file, for a CC0 sample committed next to it. Omitted when the capture this test case was checked against is an outside recording (rtl_433 test suite or Flipper Zero collection) kept out of distributed definitions; that pointer lives in the development test suite instead, matched to this entry by position.

expect.description: Expected field values, keyed by field name.

sample_rate_hz.description: Sample rate of the capture, when the file name does not state it. Older corpus files are named gfile001.cu8 with no parameters at all.

frequency_hz.description: Centre frequency of the capture, when the file name does not state it.

frame_hex.description: Expected whole frame in hexadecimal, in this definition's own bit order.

frame_symbols.description: Expected whole frame as symbols, which is the only way to state it for a non-binary alphabet such as the tri-state chips.

rtl433_tristate.description: The tri-state string rtl_433 prints for the same capture. It writes Z for the floating state where the PT2262 datasheet, and this library, write F.

rtl433_code.description: The value rtl_433 prints for the same capture, kept for traceability. A decoder there may use the opposite bit order, so this is not always equal to frame_hex.

rtl433_bit_order.description: How rtl433_code relates to frame_hex: 'same', or 'reversed' when rtl_433 reads the frame from the other end.
